Are there any practical uses of making very large transistors?

If you made one big enough, maybe you could use it instead of physical switches at power substations as seen in this application:

https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=UVF3iC_voyU

It would have to be able to handle enormous voltage differentials (~500kv) and wattage.

Although practically speaking, a physical switch would be cheaper and more reliable as they are completely passive.

Transistors, when open, still have a very small amount of resistance. This means that passing a shit-ton of current through them can heat them up, which eventually breaks them down and they lose the doping that makes them a transistor.

Larger transistors can allow for more current to pass through, but in this area the real advantages of transistors start to lose effect. A larger transistor has more gate capacitance, which makes rapid switching lossy.

If you really need to pass a super large current through transistors, you can often do it with a bank of them. This essentially allows you to create a big transistor from lots of little ones - it's good because a larger surface area lets you dissipate heat and when one transistor blows you don't have to replace the whole thing.
